title: Introduce invocation spectra profiles and SLO decision router
author: Asha Menon
release_notes: Adds invocation spectra profiling (per-invocation shape histograms) and a new SLO decision router that uses spectra to suppress noisy alerts and route degraded traffic to fallback models. No customer-facing API changes.
description: Context and motivation: We observe a high rate of noisy SLO alerts caused by short-lived bursty invocations and by phase-shifted latency (e.g., KV-cache miss warming followed by long decode tails). This PR introduces "invocation spectra" — a compact per-invocation phase-shaped profile (startup, model-attention, kv/cache, decode) — plus an in-cluster SLO decision router that uses spectra to decide whether an alert should be sent immediately, suppressed, or routed to an automated mitigation (quiet-window, fallback-model, or higher sampling for logs). The description below is a single continuous string and includes the work items, tests, and rollout plan. Work completed: - Added spectra encoder and on-path sampler in runtime that emits a 64-bit spectra fingerprint + 3-bucket per-phase histogram (serializer: protocol-buffer-lite) - Exposed spectra metrics as a new timeseries set: telemetry.invocation.spectra.shape{phase=*} and telemetry.invocation.spectra.fingerprint - Implemented slo-decision-router service that subscribes to rollup metrics and traces, evaluates rules (shape-based noise gate, cohort-specific thresholds), and emits actions to the alerting bus - Integrated router with the observability pipeline: samples for deep logs are increased for invocations flagged as 'anomalous spectra' and decreased for 'noisy short bursts' to reduce alert churn - Dashboard: new "Invocation Spectra" dashboard with sparkline lanes per phase, cohort comparison, and alert-suppression heatmap - End-to-end tests: synthetic replay bench (replaybench/spectra) with deterministic spectra shapes and unit tests for rule matching - Documentation: docs/observability/spectra.md and runbook snippet for SREs Checklist: - [x] runtime spectra encoder and unit tests - [x] metrics export + Prom/OTEL mapping - [x] slo-decision-router core logic and integration tests - [x] dashboard panels and example queries - [x] runbook and rollback steps - [x] e2e replaybench scenarios Performance and cost considerations: Spectra payload is intentionally compact (<= 64 bytes per invocation emitted at sampling rate). Default sampling is 0.5% for production routes; there is an adjustable per-route scalar. During internal load tests we observed ~2% additional ingestion cost at 1% sampling; router evaluation latency is <8ms median and <25ms 99th on a single c5-like instance. Backwards compatibility: No changes to public APIs. Metrics added are optional; old alerts continue to function. Migration: default rules are conservative (only suppress alerts with confirmed short-burst spectra and >2 coalesced violations). How it works (high level): - Runtime emits: spectra.fingerprint, spectra.shape vector, and phase-timings - Telemetry ingestion produces rollups (per-tenant, per-route spectra aggregates) - SLO decision router evaluates the incoming rollups + recent traces and writes actions to the alert bus - Alerting pipeline consults router actions before escalation and consults the router for sampling overrides for deep logs Testing summary and CI: Commits include unit tests and a replaybench job; CI initially had a flaky integration test (replaybench/large-sequences) which was fixed by adjusting the bench timeout. CI status now passing. Commits: "add spectra encoder and serializer"; "export spectra metrics to prometheus/otel"; "implement slo-decision-router basic rules"; "add dashboard and queries"; "fix replaybench timeout and stabilize tests"; "docs + runbook" Files changed (high level): - runtime/spectra/encoder.go - telemetry/collector/spectra_rolluper.go - services/slo_router/router.go - observability/dashboards/invocation_spectra.json - replaybench/spectra/benchdata/* (synthetic fixtures) - docs/observability/spectra.md - runbooks/observability/spectra-quieting.md Review conversation snapshot: "Diego: Can the router make false suppressions when phases are transient?" — Asha: "Router requires 2 consecutive rollup windows by default (configurable) and uses cohort-level baselines to avoid transient suppression." "Priya: We need to ensure spectra privacy for PII-heavy routes." — Asha: "Spectra is an aggregate phase-timing fingerprint without token content; added a configuration toggle to disable spectra emission per-tenant; documented in privacy section." "Evan: Add guardrail to prevent router from throttling all alerts for a tenant." — Asha: "Added tenant-rate guard and an emergency 'hard-override' route for oncall." Approvals: Priya (approved), Diego (approved with minor comments), Evan (approved). Merge and rollout: Merged via squash on 2026-02-25. Gradual rollout: initial sync rollout to internal and 10% of production routes for 48 hours, monitor alert volume and router decisions, then 100% if stable. Observability and SLO impact: Early experiments reduced noisy alert volume by ~28% on canary tenants with negligible increase in missed actionable alerts. Follow-ups planned: - Add ML-based spectra clustering for adaptive cohorting (ENG-9021) - Per-tenant tuning UI in Console (PM/design work) - Add offline anomaly scoring to the replaybench for historical backfills Security & compliance notes: spectra emission can be disabled per-tenant and all spectra messages are tagged with tenant IDs only after KMS tokenization; no token-level content is emitted. Rollback plan: disable router via feature-flag, revert sampling to 0, and remove router actions from alerting bus. Contact: @asha (Slack) for post-merge incidents.
